subproblem.title: Fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on a set of positive local measure (parent step 7c)
subproblem.statement: Vanishing from zero weighted integrals. Data: P ∈ ℕ; a (Borel) measure μ on ℝ^P; U, M ⊆ ℝ^P; h : ℝ^P → ℝ. Hypotheses: U is open; M ⊆ U; M is measurable; h is continuous on M; μ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; μ(M ∩ B_s(x)) > 0 for every x ∈ M and every s > 0 (B_s(x) the open ball); and ∫_M φ·h dμ = 0 for every C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ U. Conclusion: h(x) = 0 for every x ∈ M.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (U M : Set (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → MeasurableSet M → ContinuousOn h M → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < μ (M ∩ ball x s)) → (∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ U → ∫ x in M, φ x * h x ∂μ = 0) → ∀ x ∈ M, h x = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step (7c) of the supplied proof of the parent: "Suppose div_M ν(x₀) ≠ 0 for some x₀ ∈ M, and let σ ∈ {±1} be its sign. By (7a) there are c, s > 0 with closedBall(x₀, 2s) ⊆ O ∩ U and σ·div_M ν ≥ c on M ∩ B_{2s}(x₀). Take φ ∈ C^∞_c(B_{2s}(x₀); [0, 1]) with φ = 1 on B_s(x₀). Then σφ·div_M ν ≥ 0 on M and ≥ c on M ∩ B_s(x₀), so σ∫_M φ·div_M ν dH^m ≥ c·H^m(M ∩ B_s(x₀)) > 0 … This contradicts (7b)", together with the integrability remark of (7b). Here div_M ν is replaced by an arbitrary h continuous on M, H^m by μ and O ∩ U by U, and the positivity of μ(M ∩ B_s(x)) is a hypothesis (in the parent it comes from the density-one property of M).

1. (Reduction.) Suppose h(x₀) ≠ 0 for some x₀ ∈ M and let σ ∈ {1, −1} be the sign of h(x₀). The function σh satisfies every hypothesis (it is continuous on M, and ∫_M φ·σh dμ = σ∫_M φ·h dμ = 0 for every admissible φ) and σh(x₀) = |h(x₀)| > 0. Replacing h by σh we may assume h(x₀) > 0; put c := h(x₀)/2 > 0.

2. (A small ball.) Since h is continuous on M at x₀, there is δ > 0 with |h(x) − h(x₀)| < c, hence c < h(x) < 3c, for every x ∈ M with |x − x₀| < δ. Since U is open and x₀ ∈ M ⊆ U, choose r ∈ (0, δ] with B_r(x₀) ⊆ U.

3. (A bump function.) There is a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with φ = 1 on B_{r/4}(x₀) and φ = 0 outside B_{r/2}(x₀) (a smooth bump function, e.g. Mathlib ContDiffBump centred at x₀ with radii r/4 < r/2). Its topological support is contained in K := closedBall(x₀, r/2), which is compact and contained in B_r(x₀) ⊆ U. So φ has compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ U, and by hypothesis ∫_M φ·h dμ = 0.

4. (Integrability.) μ(M ∩ K) < ∞ because K is compact and K ⊆ U. The function φ·h is continuous on the measurable set M (φ is continuous and h is continuous on M), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for μ restricted to M. For x ∈ M: if x ∉ K then φ(x) = 0; if x ∈ K then |x − x₀| ≤ r/2 < δ, so 0 < h(x) < 3c and 0 ≤ φ(x)h(x) ≤ 3c. Hence 0 ≤ φh ≤ 3c·1_K on M, and φh is integrable over M since ∫_M 3c·1_K dμ = 3c·μ(M ∩ K) < ∞.

5. (Positivity.) On M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀) we have φ = 1 and h > c, so φh ≥ c; on the rest of M, φh ≥ 0 (step 4). Since M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀) is measurable with μ(M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀)) ≤ μ(M ∩ K) < ∞,
 ∫_M φ·h dμ ≥ ∫_{M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀)} φ·h dμ ≥ c·μ(M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀)) > 0,
 using the hypothesis μ(M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀)) > 0. This contradicts step 3.

6. Hence h(x) = 0 for every x ∈ M. ∎
proof_key_steps: If h(x₀) ≠ 0, replace h by −h if necessary, so that h > c > 0 on M near x₀ by continuity on M.
A C^∞ bump φ ∈ [0, 1], equal to 1 on B_{r/4}(x₀) and supported in closedBall(x₀, r/2) ⊆ U, is an admissible test function.
φh is integrable on M (bounded, supported in a compact subset of U of finite measure) and ≥ c on M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀), so ∫_M φh ≥ c·μ(M ∩ B_{r/4}(x₀)) > 0, a contradiction.

audit.reason: The proof explicitly bounds h on the chosen small neighborhood, establishes measurability and integrability of the bump-weighted function using finite compact-slice measure, and obtains a strictly positive integral from positive local measure. This contradicts the exact test-function hypothesis.
